PLAYGROUND LESSON · PLAYGROUND · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Slide — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the slide’s two golden rules — feet first, one at a time — and the whoosh that makes the waiting worth it.

What is this?

Slide is the playground’s gift ride: climb up, sit at the top, feet first down the slope, land at the bottom, clear away — and the turn-taking is part of the ride.

What does it mean?

The slide is where the playground’s social rules meet its physics: feet first (gravity’s rule), one at a time (everyone’s rule), clear away (the next rider’s rule). Three rules, total harmony, maximum whoosh.

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs three slide ideas: feet FIRST, always — sitting up or headfirst is the one no; one rider at a time — the slide is a queue, and the queue is fair; and clear away at the bottom — the next whoosh is waiting behind you.

Why this matters

The slide teaches turn-taking at its most tempting moment — when waiting is hardest — which is exactly why it works: the whoosh rewards the queue.

What it teaches

Turn-taking under excitement, body positioning (feet-first sitting), the clear-away habit, and the climb-slide-repeat rhythm that builds patience plus courage.

Words to learn

slidefeet firstturnwaitwhooshclear awayqueue

Say this to your child

“"The slide has two golden rules and one big whoosh! Feet FIRST down the slope — your feet are the brakes, so they go first. ONE rider at a time — wait your turn in the queue, it is fair for everybody. Land, stand, clear away — the next whoosh is waiting! Climb… sit… whoosh… again!"”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "This is slide — the whoosh machine!"
  2. Rule one: feet FIRST — sit at the top, feet point down the slope, hands holding the sides. Never headfirst — the feet are the brakes.
  3. Rule two: ONE at a time — wait until the rider before has landed and cleared. The queue is fair for everybody.
  4. Rule three: clear away — land, stand up, step aside: the next whoosh is waiting.
  5. Play the slide rhythm below and close: "feet first, one at a time, clear away."

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "Slide" stands in big navy capitals inside the rounded frame, with a friendly sliding illustration below — exactly as the feet-first whoosh looks.

Ask your child

"What goes first — feet or head? How many riders at once? What do we do at the bottom?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say: "Feet first — the brakes!" "One at a time, then me!" or the whoosh report: "Cleared away — next rider, go!"

Out in the real world

Slides wait in every playground — and the three rules travel to every one of them, whatever their height. The clear-away habit even works at the top of stairs.

Try it together

Slide Queue Rhythm: at the slide, practise the full rhythm out loud — climb up, sit top, FEET FIRST, whoosh, land, clear away, "next!" — three rounds each with counting turns. Then the queue game: the waiters count the whooshes aloud while waiting — the counting turns waiting into watching. Feet first, one at a time, clear away: the fairest machine on the playground.

Understanding check

Ask: "What goes first? How many riders? What happens after landing?" Feet, one, clear away — three answers and the whoosh is fair.

Parent tips

Say the rules at the BOTTOM of the ladder, not the top — rules announced calmly stick better than rules shouted mid-climb. And honour the queue: the counting waiters are practising exactly the patience the slide exists to teach.

This lesson pairs with the Slide flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Playground.
